answer: finishParallel now partitions round-robin in production and reproduces T930's 11.5x at 4x3 (11.64x @ 16 threads vs 5.11x contiguous), with byte-identical node counts across thread counts — the 5.1x ceiling was the contiguous-chunk load-imbalance bug, not a hardware limit; the remaining ~2x gap to linear is memory latency.
notes: Implemented round-robin partition in RT.finishParallel (src/retro.zig): root i -> thread i % N via a permuted flat buffer, replacing the contiguous chunks. Two deliberate testing seams, no solver/orbit/writes-off change: RETRO_PARTITION=contig restores the legacy contiguous chunking (the seeded-defect control + A/B), and finishParallel now emits one per-thread node-count line to stderr (the regression's imbalance detector reads it). RETRO_4X3=1 added so the 4x3 re-measurement drives the production pipeline, not T930's throwaway harness. Regression tools/regression-finishparallel-partition.sh wired into zig build test: null control (2 serial + 2 parallel 3x3 runs byte-identical: solved=622 filled=8698 skipped=0 single-ko=11 nodes=315484, bracket-fails=0 orbit-clashes=0 symmetry=PASS) + seeded-defect control (3x3 @ 3 threads: round-robin max/mean=1.119 <= 1.40 PASS; contiguous max/mean=1.619 > 1.40 DETECTED). RED-first: a throwaway copy with the default flipped back to contiguous produced max/mean=1.619, tripping the balanced arm (<= 1.40) — the guard is not vacuous. Production 4x3 re-measurement (ReleaseFast, caffeinate held): serial 35,670 ms; rr16 3,064 ms (11.64x, T930 11.54x); contig16 6,985 ms (5.11x, T930 5.10x); rr18 3,124 ms (11.42x, T930 10.87x).
